problem: DRL object-navigation agents (e.g., MJOLNIR-o) explore and localize targets well but fail to keep approaching the target and to recognize when to terminate, especially in long-episode environments without depth; they often terminate early to avoid step penalties.
motivation: Objects differ in size, so without depth an RL agent can hardly relate its actions to the termination condition and falls into local optima (early Done). The authors observe that even after seeing the target, agents often fail to approach it and terminate correctly, and they want a termination decision that implicitly reflects object-wise distance.
key_idea: Add a supervised 'Judge Model' trained in parallel with the A3C agent, using the RL reward as the label, that implicitly infers object-wise depth from detection and image features and gates the Done action jointly with the RL policy.
insight: Termination is separated from control and learned as a supervised binary classification from reward signals (reward >= 4.0 means positive) on states where the target is visible, which gives implicit depth cues without depth sensors. The gains are largest on long episodes (L>=5: SR 50.0 to 57.9 vs MJOLNIR-o) and in large rooms like living rooms (SR 75.6 vs 50.0), supporting that better termination is the source of improvement. However, it hurts in the bathroom (SR 63.2 vs 82.4) and SPL gains are marginal. No isolated ablation of components (focal loss, largest-bbox selection) is reported.
method: Backbone DRL branch: MJOLNIR-o (GCN over object-relation graph with GloVe node features plus a Context Matrix of per-class visibility, bbox center, bbox area and cosine similarity to target) feeding an LSTM and A3C to output the control distribution P_con; modified so the largest-bbox instance represents a class instead of averaging.

Judge Model input: ResNet-18 (ImageNet) image feature ImgEmb, target row TagVec from the Context Matrix (row with CS=1.0), and target GloVe embedding are concatenated into StateEmb; only 'Effective States' where the target is visible are used.

Judge Model architecture: stacked linear expand/squeeze layers with Leaky ReLU (to avoid dead ReLU with negative GloVe values) fuse the three components and output a binary [p_d, p_n] termination distribution.

Reward-supervised parallel training: the environment reward at step t is converted to a label (R>=4.0 positive; successful episodes have R in [4.05,4.90]), stored with StateEmb in a 64-sample Batch Buffer, and the judge is updated whenever the buffer is full, in parallel with A3C; trained with Focal Loss (gamma=0.7) to handle heavy negative-class imbalance.

Action control: in training, actions are sampled from P_con. At test time, Done is output if p_d + p_lambda >= 1.5 (p_lambda is the Done probability from P_con); otherwise if p_d is sampled the action comes from P_con, and if p_n is sampled it comes from P_sub (P_con without Done).
Training schedule: judge and RL trained jointly for 1.6M episodes until judge accuracy saturates, then the judge is frozen and RL continues to 3.0M episodes total, A3C with 8 workers.

setting.backbone: MJOLNIR-o (GCN + LSTM + A3C) plus Judge Model MLP on ResNet-18 features (trained from scratch, ResNet-18 ImageNet pre-trained)
setting.training_data: Online RL interaction in 80 AI2-THOR training rooms (20 per room type), 3.0M episodes; judge trained on reward-derived labels collected online; VG object relation graph and GloVe embeddings
setting.observation: egocentric RGB with ground-truth object detector outputs (no depth)
setting.action_space: discrete: MoveAhead 0.25 m, RotateLeft/Right 45°, LookUp/Down 30°, Done
setting.privileged: ground-truth object detector (bounding boxes and classes)

numbers.eval_set_note: 40 held-out AI2-THOR rooms (10 per room type)
numbers.extra: ground-truth object detector; success if Done with target visible within 1.5 m; L>=5 column = episodes with optimal length >=5

numbers_note: Tables 1 and 2 report different aggregate values for DITA (71.4 vs 68.3 SR) and MJOLNIR-o (65.3 vs 62.6); the paper does not explain this. Split is a custom AI2-THOR 80/40 room split, not a canonical benchmark.
results: DITA reaches 71.4 SR / 21.6 SPL over all rooms versus 65.3 / 21.1 for the strongest baseline MJOLNIR-o (the abstract claims a +9.3% relative gain), and 57.9 SR on long episodes (L>=5) versus 50.0. It is best in living room (75.6 SR) and bedroom (61.5) but worse in bathroom (63.2 vs 82.4) and slightly lower in kitchen SR.
limitations: Fails when the target requires precise path planning (e.g., a pillow on a double bed in a narrow room), suggesting a need for explicit planning.
Training time is much larger than all other tested models.
Uses ground-truth object detection in a small AI2-THOR setup; no real-robot or large-scale benchmark evaluation, and no component ablations; SPL gains are marginal and bathroom performance drops.
